healthcareSystem: Universal (National Health System — primarily for residents)
qualityNotes: Excellent healthcare with well-trained doctors and modern facilities. English is universal. ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) covers accidents for all people in New Zealand — but does NOT cover illness. Public hospitals are good; private hospitals are even better but more expensive. Healthcare costs can be high for tourists.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-5:30pm weekdays. Some are open on weekends. In small towns, pharmacy hours may be limited. On-duty pharmacies cover after-hours needs.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are available in all towns and cities. Many medications require a prescription. Some common items are available OTC. Pharmacists are helpful and knowledgeable.
prescriptionRules: A New Zealand prescription is required for most medications. Foreign prescriptions are not accepted — you'll need to see a New Zealand doctor.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine products require a prescription in New Zealand since 2017. Small quantities may be available with pharmacist consultation.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring a New Zealand specialist prescription. Bringing these requires approval from the Ministry of Health.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in New Zealand. CBD oil is available by prescription for specific conditions but not to tourists generally.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. For controlled medications, contact the Ministry of Health before travel. Carry prescriptions for all medications.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Strongly recommended. ACC covers accidents but NOT illness. Healthcare for tourists can be expensive.
travelInsurance.tips: ACC covers accidents (injuries) for everyone in NZ, regardless of residency. However, illness (getting sick) is NOT covered. Travel insurance that covers medical evacuation from remote areas is essential — New Zealand's geography means evacuation from South Island or remote areas can cost $50,000+.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout New Zealand. Bottled water is also widely available.
foodSafetyTips: New Zealand has excellent food safety. Lamb, seafood, and dairy are highlights. Hangi (Māori earth oven cooking) is safe from reputable providers. Green-lipped mussels are a must-try — safe from restaurants. Watch out for food in very remote areas where refrigeration may be limited.
medicalTourismNote: New Zealand is not typically a medical tourism destination but attracts visitors for its clean image, wellness retreats, and world-class healthcare for those who can afford it.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to New Zealand. Emergency number (111), ACC accident coverage info, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Auckland City Hospital
hospitals.notes: New Zealand's largest hospital. 24/7 emergency department.

hospitals.name: Wellington Regional Hospital
hospitals.notes: Capital city hospital. Full emergency department.

hospitals.name: Christchurch Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for the South Island's largest city.

hospitals.name: Queenstown Lakes District Hospital
hospitals.notes: Serves the Queenstown adventure tourism area. Handles adventure sport injuries.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care but expensive. Not covered by public healthcare for adults.
dentalCare.costRange: NZD $80-150 for consultation; NZD $150-400 for fillings; NZD $200-500 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Dental care in New Zealand is high quality but costly. Emergency dental care available in major cities. Most dentists accept walk-ins for emergencies.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Call Healthline at 0800 611 116 for dental emergency advice. Hospital emergency departments handle dental trauma.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 1737 (Need to talk? — free, 24/7, call or text)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Widely available. English is the primary language.
mentalHealth.notes: New Zealand has good mental health services. Crisis support available 24/7. GPs can provide mental health referrals. Private therapy: NZD $120-200 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: New Zealand has good accessibility in cities and major tourist attractions. Adventure activities and natural sites may have limitations.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: All public hospitals are wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses in major cities are accessible. Mobility parking widely available. Some interisland ferries are accessible. Domestic flights accommodate wheelchairs.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Many Great Walks have sections accessible to wheelchair users. Milford Sound cruises are accessible. Adventure activity operators in Queenstown increasingly offer adaptive options. CCS Disability Action provides travel information.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.testing: RATs available at pharmacies. PCR available at GP clinics.
covidStatus.notes: New Zealand removed all COVID entry restrictions. The main health risks for travelers are adventure sports injuries and sun exposure.

insuranceClaimProcess: ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) covers treatment for injuries sustained in New Zealand, including tourists — at no cost. For illness (non-injury), keep all receipts and GP notes for insurance claims. NZ healthcare for non-residents is not free for illness-related treatment.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower (or free for residents). Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Local hospitals handle the vast majority of cases — air evacuation is rarely needed for tourists. If a condition exceeds local capacity: Australian and New Zealand hospitals are among the best globally. Inter-city air evacuation is well-developed.

drugNameMap.note: The dominant Commonwealth brand. Generic 'paracetamol' also widely sold.
